newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS - New issues add to dull session.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS - New issues add to dull session.

text.p: U.S. high-grade secondary corporate trade endured another dull session Wednesday as players focused mostly on new debt issues and this week's key release of U.S. employment data, dealers said.
"We're still marking time before the (U.S.) employment numbers so we haven't seen much activity today," said a high-grade trader.
Friday, Labor Department is scheduled to release U.S. payrolls/unemployment figures for May.
In a Reuter poll, U.S. economist forecast a 5.0 percent unemployment rate and an increase of 219,000 in payrolls.
In the corporate primary sector, Ford Motor unit Ford Motor Credit Corp issued $1.0 billion in A1/A-plus rated 10-year global debt via Merrill Lynch & Co.
The deal was marketed with price talk of around 60 basis points but priced at 59 basis points over Treasuries due to strong demand from global investors, a Merrill official said.
Market sources noted international investors have shown a strong appetite for 10-year paper, the longest maturity in which they typically invest.
Still, another $1.75 billion in global debt offerings is expected to hit the market, syndicate sources said.
Those include a $1.0 billion 10-year global debt offering from Bayerische Landesbank and a $750 million 10-year global 144A debt offering from Rheinische Hyppothekenbank, players said.

Among other issues, Banco do Brasil sold $200 million in five-year notes at 200 basis points over Treasuries and another $200 million in 10-year notes at 287.5 basis points via joint managers UBS Securities and BB Securities.
Meanwhile, players said Tuesday's banking issues were seen trading at a tighter spread in the secondary market.
"Yesterday's banking issues did very well...they tightened one to two basis points in the aftermarket," a high-grade trader said.
Among those issuers were BBT&T Corp, Citicorp and Comerica unit, Comerica Bank, which successfully sold $650 million in new debt.
Turning to the high-yield sector, D.R. Horton, a builder of single family homes, sold $150 million in 8-3/8 percent seven-year notes via Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette.
ICO Inc also sold $120 million in 10-year 144A notes at 374.5 basis points over Treasuries, sources said.

Also, Pennsylvania oil refining company United Refining Co tapped the market with $200 million in 10-year senior notes to yield 10-3/4 percent. Dillon Read & Co was lead manager for the deal, sources said.
In the secondary junk sector, prices wound down the day up 1/4 in moderate trade, high-yield players said.
Flagstar Cos 10-7/8 percent paper fared better trading up one point higher at 100-5/8 bid, 100-3/4 offer. The 10-3/4 debt was also bid up one point at 100-1/2, 100-3/4 offer, traders said.
Among supermarket paper, Grand Union 12 percent notes were quoted off 1/4 at 76-1/4 bid, 76-1/2 offer.
Also, Penn Traffic ended a volatile session off 1/4 after recouping some earlier losses, players said.
"Penn 9-5/8's traded below 50 bid today but they've come back to trade at 51-3/4 bid, 51-7/8 offer, 1/4 off on the day, one trader of distressed debt said.
In the U.S. governments market, the benchmark 30-year T-bond closed down 5/32 at 96-24/32 to yield 6.88 percent.
